theme: Hotel supply data: Overture/OSM hotel POI counts, hotel pipeline datasets, lodging census (Census QSS NAICS 721), county business patterns tooling
queries_run: gh search repos "overture maps places hotel"
gh search repos "STR census QSS lodging"
gh search repos "quarterly services survey lodging"
gh search repos "hotel construction pipeline STR"

candidates.name: OvertureMaps/data
candidates.what_it_holds: Root repo/pointer for the Overture Maps Foundation open dataset: six themes (addresses, base, buildings, divisions, places, transportation) released as cloud-native GeoParquet on S3/Azure, monthly-ish releases since mid-2023 (STAC catalog tracks each release). The 'places' theme includes global POIs with a category taxonomy (accommodation/lodging/hotel/motel/hostel categories, brand, confidence score, lat/lon, open/close dates in later releases) built from Meta, Microsoft, TomTom, Esri and community contributions. Not committed as files in-repo; pulled via `overturemaps` CLI or DuckDB spatial extension (one command: `overturemaps download --type=place --bbox=... `).
candidates.why_useful: A repeatable, versioned pull of global hotel/lodging POI counts and locations by release date is a direct, non-Airbnb proxy for hotel-supply growth or contraction by market — fills gap 8 (hotel supply/demand) and gap 20 (geospatial POI). Because releases are dated snapshots, diffing releases gives a point-in-time hotel-count series per city/country that could be compared against ABNB listing growth in the same markets.
candidates.size_hint: Places theme alone is 100M+ POIs globally (multi-GB per release); filterable by bbox/category before download

candidates.name: OvertureMaps/schema
candidates.what_it_holds: Formal schema definitions for the Overture places theme, including the category taxonomy (accommodation > hotel, motel, hostel, bed_and_breakfast, resort etc.) needed to correctly filter the OvertureMaps/data pull for lodging-only POIs.
candidates.why_useful: Needed alongside OvertureMaps/data to write a correct category filter for hotel/lodging extraction; not standalone data but the map key that makes the pull usable.

candidates.name: healthyregions/overture-poi-extract
candidates.what_it_holds: Simple script (DuckDB-based) for creating geojson/shp/pmtiles extracts from the Overture Maps POI dataset for a chosen bbox/category — i.e. a ready-made recipe for pulling just the hotel/lodging POI subset instead of writing the DuckDB query from scratch.
candidates.why_useful: Lowers the effort to turn OvertureMaps/data into a usable hotel-POI-by-city extract; CC0 licensed so no reuse friction.
candidates.time_coverage: Whatever Overture release is current when run

candidates.name: yharby/OvertureMapsDownloader
candidates.what_it_holds: Wraps DuckDB, Dask and GDAL/OGR to download and manipulate Overture Maps data (any theme, including places) into common GIS formats; 103 stars, actively maintained.
candidates.why_useful: Alternative, more general-purpose puller for the same hotel-POI-by-release data as OvertureMaps/data; useful if the official CLI's bbox/format options are insufficient.

candidates.name: ar-puuk/overture-data-download
candidates.what_it_holds: R + DuckDB script to download Overture Maps Foundation data (places/buildings/etc.) for a given area of interest.
candidates.why_useful: R-based alternative acquisition method for the same hotel-POI source; only useful if the team's pipeline is R rather than Python.

candidates.name: arthurgailes/overtureR
candidates.what_it_holds: R package that loads Overture Maps datasets as dbplyr/sf-ready data frames (21 stars), i.e. an R client library for the same places/hotel POI data.
candidates.why_useful: Makes the Overture places (hotel/lodging) pull scriptable and joinable in R for anyone building the hotel-supply proxy in R rather than Python/DuckDB directly.

candidates.name: whubsch/overturetoosm
candidates.what_it_holds: Python package translating Overture Maps schema/tags to OpenStreetMap tags (and vice versa conceptually), useful for cross-walking Overture's accommodation categories to OSM's tourism=hotel/motel/hostel/guest_house tagging scheme.
candidates.why_useful: Lets a hotel-supply build reconcile counts pulled from Overture with counts pulled directly from OSM (Overpass/Geofabrik extracts), giving two independent POI sources to cross-check a hotel-count time series.

candidates.name: jtilly/cbpR
candidates.what_it_holds: R package that downloads and assembles panel datasets from the U.S. Census Bureau's County Business Patterns (CBP) program, aggregable to county/metro/micro level; `getFirmCount()`-style functions accept a NAICS code (demonstrated with a 6-digit code, so NAICS 721 'Accommodation' / 721110 'Hotels and Motels' is selectable), and years are user-specified (demo shown for 2000-2009, but CBP itself runs 1986-2023 annual).
candidates.why_useful: CBP publishes annual county-level establishment counts, employment and payroll for NAICS 721 (Accommodation and Food Services > Accommodation) — a free, long-run, granular US hotel-supply census (number of hotel establishments, employment) that could be turned into a US hotel-supply-growth series to compare against Airbnb's US listing growth. Directly addresses gap 8 (hotel supply) with public, county-level government data going back further than any commercial STR/CoStar series we hold.
candidates.time_coverage: CBP program spans 1986-2023 annually; package demo covers 2000-2009 but is not hardcoded to that range
candidates.size_hint: Tooling + cached CBP panel builds, CBP source files are tens of MB/year

candidates.name: dvrpc/economic-subsectors
candidates.what_it_holds: Analyzes 3-digit NAICS subsectors (industries incl. accommodation) at the county/regional level using County Business Patterns (CBP), Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages (QCEW), and Current Population Survey (CPS) data for the Delaware Valley (Philadelphia) region; committed processing code plus regional extracts.
candidates.why_useful: A worked example of joining CBP + QCEW for a NAICS subsector, showing how to build a regional hotel-establishment/employment series; useful as a code template even though the region (Philadelphia metro) is narrow.
candidates.time_coverage: Not specified in listing, recent CBP/QCEW vintages

candidates.name: Zarco-ai/Harris-CBP-2023-Audit
candidates.what_it_holds: Cleaned, row-by-row-verified Census County Business Patterns 2023 extract for Harris County, TX (Houston), with an audit trail correcting a size-class double-count bug in an AI-generated pipeline; includes the corrected CBP-2023 dataset by NAICS code for that county (would include 721 Accommodation rows).
candidates.why_useful: A single-county, single-year worked/QA'd CBP 2023 extract — useful mainly as a sanity-check reference for how to correctly parse CBP size-class fields (a known gotcha) rather than as broad coverage; Houston is not a top ABNB market.

candidates.name: OvertureMaps/explore-site
candidates.what_it_holds: Interactive web map for exploring Overture Maps data themes (including places/accommodation) release-by-release; points at the same S3/Azure-hosted Parquet releases as OvertureMaps/data, useful only for eyeballing coverage before committing to a bulk pull.
candidates.why_useful: Quick visual QA of hotel POI density/coverage in specific ABNB markets before investing in the DuckDB pull.

candidates.name: OvertureMaps/stac
candidates.what_it_holds: Generates STAC (SpatioTemporal Asset Catalog) manifest files cataloguing every dated Overture Maps release, giving a machine-readable index of release dates back to the dataset's start.
candidates.why_useful: Gives the exact list of release timestamps needed to build a point-in-time hotel-POI-count time series (one count per release date) rather than only the latest snapshot — relevant to the point-in-time rule this project enforces.

notes: gh search repos returned zero hits for several natural-language multi-word queries ("hotel pipeline dataset", "NAICS 721 hotel", "osm hotel poi", "overture maps places hotel", "STR census QSS lodging", "quarterly services survey lodging", "hotel construction pipeline STR") — the search API appears to AND all terms literally rather than doing fuzzy/OR matching, so specific phrase queries starve; broader single/double-word queries ("overture maps", "county business patterns") worked much better. No repo found for: Census QSS (Quarterly Services Survey) NAICS 721 lodging specifically (QSS revenue data seems to have no GitHub tooling — it's a small BEA/Census series usually pulled by hand); STR/CoStar hotel pipeline/construction datasets (these are paid, proprietary, and unsurprisingly absent from open GitHub); no OSM-specific (Overpass/Geofabrik) hotel-extraction repo surfaced in this run's queries — Overture Maps effectively supersedes ad-hoc OSM hotel scraping since it already ingests OSM plus Meta/Microsoft/TomTom/Esri place data with a clean accommodation category, so it is the stronger lead for gap 8/20. Recommend a follow-up scout specifically try `gh search repos "overpass hotel"`, `gh search repos "tourism hotel geofabrik"`, and `gh search repos "AHLA STR data"` under its own budget. Also worth flagging to the CBP-focused workstream: CBP county data undercounts short-term-rental-adjacent categories (NAICS 721199 'All Other Traveler Accommodation' vs 721110 'Hotels/Motels') — a real hotel-supply build needs to pick the right 6-digit code, which none of the tooling repos found here do automatically.
